newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Western Areas knocked by JCI's results.
newsitem.headline: Western Areas knocked by JCI's results.

text.p: South African mining house Western Areas' shares dropped 9.6 percent on Wednesday after its holding company JCI posted poor gold quarterly results on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Well, it is down on the results," one dealer said.
"It looks like the share has got a re-rating here. JCI is also down, it also fell yesterday (Tuesday) after the results were released," the dealer added.
JCI, which has two other mines, reported a 67 percent drop in profit to 44.24 million rand in the March quarter from 132.89 million in the three months to December, 1996.
Gold production fell by 8.9 percent to 10,676kg from 11,724kg in the previous quarter.
By 1159 GMT Western Areas' stock tumbled 425 cents to 40.00 rand with shares valued at over 600,000 rand changing hands. while JCI was down 95 cents to 40.75 rands.
Dealers, however, said Western Areas' gloom could soon be over as more market players were starting to discount most of the gold results.
